blocks.text: Truth tables are used in logic to show the truth values of statements. They help us understand how logical expressions work. A truth table lists all possible combinations of truth values. It shows the final result for each combination. Truth tables are important in propositional logic. They are widely used in computer science and mathematics. They help in checking the correctness of logical expressions. Truth tables make logical thinking clear and simple (as shown in Figure 2.5).

blocks.caption: Figure 2.5: Truth Table for Logical Expressions

blocks.text: The main purpose of truth tables is to show how a logical expression behaves. They help us find when a statement is true or false. Truth tables list all possible input values. They help remove confusion in logical reasoning. Using truth tables, we can check complex expressions easily. They help compare different logical statements. Truth tables are useful in decision-making. They are important tools in logic and computer science.
Creating Truth Tables for Logical Expressions

Creating a truth table starts with identifying the propositions. Each proposition is given a truth value of true or false. All possible combinations of truth values are listed. Logical connectives are applied step by step. The final result is written for each row. This process helps to understand the expression clearly. Truth tables must be neat and organized. They are easy to follow and use.

Each proposition P or Q can take the value True (T) or False (F). Truth tables enumerate all possible combinations (2ⁿ rows for n propositions). Truth value of a compound proposition is determined by the values of its components.
